item.title: Tata Motors' Iveco bid crosses 80% threshold as acceptances hit 87.81%
item.description: Provisional acceptances under the €3.91 billion offer reached 87.81 per cent of Iveco's share capital, clearing the revised minimum threshold of 80 per cent ...
item.dc:creator: Shine Jacob
item.content:encoded: Tata Motors’ takeover bid for Iveco has crossed the key acceptance threshold of 80 per cent, clearing a major hurdle for the acquisition of the Italian truck maker by the Indian commercial vehicle major. Tata Motors on Monday secured provisional acceptances for 87.81 per cent of Iveco Group’s share capital under its €3.91 billion takeover offer. This will take Tata Motors’ shareholding in Iveco to 89.42 per cent. The move paves the way for further expansion of Tata Motors into global markets and its entry into new product segments. The acquisition was first announced in July last year and had faced several roadblocks over the past 15 months. At an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) on October 16, around 53 per cent reportedly voted in favour of the deal, while 12 per cent were against it and 35 per cent did not vote. Shareholders approved all resolutions proposed by the board, including lowering the minimum tender acceptance threshold from 95 per cent to 80 per cent. “As part of the public tender offer (OPA) launched by Tata Motors for Iveco ordinary shares, 97,078,765 applications were submitted today, October 26, the last day for acceptances. Therefore, overall acceptance requests reach 238,157,212, equal to approximately 87.81 per cent of the total instruments being offered,” Iveco said in a stock market filing. Final results will be communicated before market opening on October 29. Iveco said the offer is set to be reopened during November 2-6. The tender offer, which ended on Monday, had started on September 7. The offer was made by TML CV Holdings, an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Tata Motors. The price for each common share tendered in acceptance of the offer consists of the initial price indicated in the offer document of €14.10, cum dividend, increased by an additional €0.30, cum dividend. The aggregate offer price is therefore €14.40 per common share, according to the statement. The deal, which was initially expected to be completed by June this year, was postponed due to delays in regulatory approvals. For Tata Motors, whose commercial vehicle division currently derives nearly 90 per cent of its revenue from India, the acquisition represents a strategic expansion into new geographies. The two companies will have combined annual sales volumes of more than 540,000 vehicles and revenue of over $25 billion. Iveco has an established presence across Europe, Latin America and Asia-Pacific, with production facilities in Europe, China, Russia, Australia and Latin America, and a network spanning 160 countries. Iveco’s annual revenue of around €10 billion is expected to significantly increase Tata Motors’ commercial vehicle scale, while adding electric buses, electric light commercial vehicles and alternative-fuel technologies to its portfolio. The acquisition could nearly triple Tata Motors’ commercial vehicle revenue from the current Rs 77,000 crore to more than Rs 2 trillion, according to experts.

item.title: Harry Kane ends England's 25-year Ballon d'Or wait after 73-goal season
item.description: From difficult loan spells to Bayern Munich's attacking fulcrum, Kane's first Ballon d'Or crowns a career built against expectation and makes him England's first winner since Michael Owen ...
item.dc:creator: Anish Kumar
item.content:encoded: Harry Kane’s heart was racing. Before he could get his hands on the Ballon d’Or, he had to hear his name from Ronaldo, a footballer he had idolised growing up. Then came the moment that ended a quarter of a century’s wait for an English winner. At the London Palladium, the 33-year-old Bayern Munich striker won the men’s 2026 Ballon d’Or for his performances in 2025-26, becoming the first Englishman to claim the award since Michael Owen in 2001. A season of 73 goals had taken him past his rivals; a career spent challenging expectations had brought him to this stage. Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappe finished second, while Barcelona’s World Cup winner Lamine Yamal was third. Kane, who had already collected the men’s striker of the year award earlier in the evening, was also Bayern’s first Ballon d’Or winner since Karl-Heinz Rummenigge’s successive triumphs in 1980 and 1981. “Oh, there were so many emotions. My heart was beating fast, and I was just hoping that he would say my name,” Kane said after the ceremony. “Ronaldo was one of my idols growing up.” Receiving the trophy from the former Brazil forward made the occasion even more special. Surrounded by friends and family, Kane described a rush of memories and emotions that went beyond what he had imagined. From uncertain loan spells to football’s summit There had been little certainty about this destination when Kane was a teenager. His early career took him on loan to Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich City and Leicester City. Those difficult spells offered few guarantees that a player once considered below Premier League standard would eventually stand among the game’s most celebrated names. Kane came through Tottenham Hotspur’s youth ranks and spent 14 seasons in the first team. He left as the club’s record scorer with 280 goals. His 213 Premier League goals put him second on the competition’s all-time list, behind Alan Shearer’s 260. In the summer of 2023, Bayern paid more than €100 million to take him to Germany. Three full seasons later, Kane is already seventh among the club’s all-time scorers. He also became the fastest player to reach 100 Bundesliga goals, getting there in 98 matches. For England, he is the all-time leading scorer, joint-most capped player and a World Cup Golden Boot winner. The outstanding English footballer of his generation now has the individual award to match that standing. A 73-goal season, with only Messi ahead Kane’s case for the Ballon d’Or rested on an extraordinary volume of work: 73 goals in 65 appearances for club and country. Only Lionel Messi has scored more in a single season this century, with 82 goals in 2011-12. At Bayern, Kane’s 36 goals in 31 Bundesliga appearances helped secure another league title. The champions lost just once and finished 16 points clear of second-placed Borussia Dortmund. The German Cup final supplied a particularly emphatic finish to the domestic campaign. Kane scored all three goals as Bayern beat Stuttgart 3-0, completing a league-and-cup double. They also won the German Super Cup. In the Champions League, he contributed 14 goals in 13 appearances. Bayern’s European run ended with a narrow semi-final defeat to eventual champions Paris Saint-Germain. Harry Kane’s 2025-26 season in numbersKane scored 61 goals for Bayern Munich and 12 for England, finishing with 73 goals in 65 appearances.TeamCompetitionAppearancesGoalsBayern MunichBundesliga3136Bayern MunichChampions League1314Bayern MunichGerman Cup (DFB-Pokal)610Bayern MunichGerman Super Cup11Bayern Munich subtotalAll club competitions5161EnglandWorld Cup finals76EnglandWorld Cup qualifiers55EnglandInternational friendlies21England subtotalAll internationals1412Overall totalClub and country6573 More than the player at the finish The goals explain the scale of Kane’s season. His influence on Bayern’s football explains its distinction. He had already become an unusually versatile centre-forward at Tottenham, able to create chances and shape attacks as well as finish them. In Munich, the players around him gave those qualities greater room to flourish. At Spurs, his understanding with Son Heung-min often operated as an isolated partnership, particularly in their later seasons together. Bayern offered a broader network: Michael Olise to his right, Luis Diaz to his left and players of the highest quality alongside and behind him. Kane could lead the line, move into attacking midfield or drop deeper to direct play. His connection with those around him helped make Bayern, at their best, one of the most compelling attacking teams to watch. There were moments that captured both sides of his game. Against Real Madrid at the Bernabeu, he finished a sweeping counter-attack with an elegant side-footed strike. In the next round, at the Parc des Princes, his lofted pass over the Paris Saint-Germain defence released Diaz for one of the European season’s finest goals. The range of Kane’s game had been evident before his move. Bayern gave it a fuller expression, allowing him to influence how the entire attack worked. Six World Cup goals and an English milestone The summer brought another substantial contribution for England, even as the country’s 60-year wait for a World Cup title continued. Kane scored six goals as England finished third at the tournament in the US, Canada and Mexico. His double rescued them from the prospect of a humiliating last-16 exit against DR Congo, securing a 2-1 victory. He then scored a crucial goal in the 3-2 quarter-final win over co-hosts Mexico. His Ballon d’Or campaign therefore reached its conclusion without either a World Cup triumph or a Champions League winners’ medal — team honours that so often strengthen a contender’s case. At 33, a season of this quality offered a precious opening. The award recognised the sustained excellence of his contribution across teams and competitions, giving his achievement a significance beyond the medals Bayern and England had collected. “It’s massive for England, for our country,” Kane said. He described London as a good omen and spoke of the long wait since the country’s previous winner. Having grown up watching great English players, he was proud to put England back alongside the trophy and pointed to the quality of the country’s current footballers. “Playing for England is my biggest honour, the thing I love to do the most. So to represent my country in this way is truly amazing.” A message for Kompany, a tribute to Kate Kane’s acceptance speech also turned towards people whose contributions could not be measured in goals. He thanked his team-mates, coaches and family, and sent a message to Bayern manager Vincent Kompany, who is recovering after collapsing at the club’s training ground last week. “To Vinny, I know he is at home or still in the hospital. Wishing you well. I hope this gave you a bit of energy,” Kane said. He closed by addressing his three children and paying tribute to his wife, Kate. “My wife Kate, my best friend. You’re my biggest supporter. We have done it,” he said. Kane spoke of her wish to see him succeed and the sacrifices she had made to help him pursue his ambitions, adding: “It wouldn’t be possible without you.” Putellas returns to the top with third award Alexia Putellas shared the evening’s leading honours, winning the women’s Ballon d’Or for a record-equalling third time. The 32-year-old reclaimed the award from her Spain team-mate Aitana Bonmati, as she and Kane were crowned the world’s best footballers at the London ceremony. Yamal was also among the young player award winners, while Barcelona Femeni and Paris Saint-Germain took the club honours. Ballon d’Or 2026: The award winnersAwardWinner or winnersMen’s Ballon d’OrHarry KaneWomen’s Ballon d’OrAlexia PutellasYoung playersLopez and Lamine YamalCoachesRomeu and De la FuenteGoalkeepersColl and SimonClubsBarcelona Femeni and Paris Saint-GermainTop scorersCorral and Harry Kane For Kane, the night brought a career of resistance to early judgements into its sharpest focus. The teenager who had moved between loan clubs was now receiving football’s most coveted individual prize from one of his heroes. This time, when Ronaldo said his name, there was a Ballon d’Or waiting.

item.description: The five-day nationwide poll also showed that registered voters broadly favored Democrats over Republicans by 47% to 36% when asked which party they would pick for Congress ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / Trump approval rises from record low to 32% ahead of midterm election: Poll

Trump approval rises from record low to 32% ahead of midterm election: Poll The five-day nationwide poll also showed that registered voters broadly favored Democrats over Republicans by 47% to 36% when asked which party they would pick for Congress

Trump's fellow Republicans are fighting to retain the party's majorities in the House of Representatives and Senate during midterm elections (Photo:PTI)

Reuters WASHINGTON 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 27 2026 | 8:40 AM IST

Listen to This Article

US President Donald Trump's public approval rating inched higher to 32%, up a percentage point from last week's record low, ahead of the November 3 midterm elections that will decide which party controls Congress, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on Monday.   Trump's fellow Republicans are fighting to retain the party's majorities in the House of Representatives and Senate.   The five-day nationwide poll also showed that registered voters broadly favored Democrats over Republicans by 47% to 36% when asked which party they would pick for Congress in what is known as a "generic ballot" question. Some 11% said they did not know who they would vote for if the election were held today.

That gap of 11 percentage points between Democrats and Republicans was 1 percentage point tighter than in a Reuters/Ipsos poll that closed on October 19. The latest poll additionally asked undecided voters which party they were leaning toward. Factoring in their responses, the national race appeared somewhat tighter, with Democrats leading by 9 percentage points, 50% to 41%.   For Republicans, losing control of either chamber could complicate Trump's agenda in the last two years of his second term as president. Also Read

'Looked so corrupt, terrible': Trump questions Brazil election integrity

Trump admin eyes Hungarian PM Orbán for UN chief with Russia, China backing

Trump adds Norway to vulgar list of countries over Nobel Peace Prize snub

'I had to do it': Trump says US-Canada tariff dispute to end 'soon'

Trump names Vance, Rubio among potential 2028 Republican candidates

Generic ballot polls are national polls that provide an overall view of which party poll respondents would like to see in charge in Congress. While these polls provide a view of national public sentiment, they do not capture the nuances of the state-by-state and district-by-district contests that determine control of the Senate and House, contests in which Republicans hold some structural advantages.

STEEP SENATE CLIMB FOR DEMOCRATS   Political analysts generally see the Democrats having a good chance of winning control of the House, but think they face a steeper climb to win the Senate.   It remains to be seen how many voters will actually cast ballots. The voters who appeared most likely to vote still favored Democrats over Republicans by 9 points, 53% to 44%.   The fight for Congress has appeared to turn on views around inflation, which has surged since Trump ordered military strikes on Iran in February that sent gasoline prices higher. Some 73% of voters in the poll said their cost of living was heading in the wrong direction.

Prior to the start of the war, Reuters/Ipsos polls showed voters preferring Republicans over Democrats as the better stewards of the US economy. The latest poll showed 37% of voters said Democrats have a better approach on the economy, compared to 33% who picked Republicans on the issue.   The poll also suggested Democratic voters were more excited about voting, with 46% of Democrats saying they were very enthusiastic about the midterms, compared to 30% of Republicans who said the same.   The Reuters/Ipsos poll, which was conducted online, gathered responses from 1,679 US adults, including 1,280 registered voters, and had a margin of error of 2 percentage points for all adults and 3 points for registered voters.

Home / World News / US judge rejects Novo Nordisk bid to halt Eli Lilly's weight-loss drug ads

US judge rejects Novo Nordisk bid to halt Eli Lilly's weight-loss drug ads Weight-loss drugs have become major businesses for large pharmaceutical companies. The US is among a handful of countries that allow direct-to-consumer advertising of prescription medicines

Novo Nordisk sued Eli Lilly in July, saying ads for the obesity drug Zepbound and diabetes treatment Mounjaro violated federal and state false advertising and unfair competition laws by comparing higher doses of those products with lower doses of Novo Nordisk's Wegovy and Ozempic (Photo: Reuters)

Reuters 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 27 2026 | 8:36 AM IST

Listen to This Article

A US judge rejected on Monday Novo Nordisk's request to block Eli Lilly from continuing advertisements for weight-loss drugs that the Danish drugmaker considered false and misleading, affecting markets with tens of billions of dollars of annual sales.   US District Judge Zahid Quraishi in Trenton, New Jersey, said Novo Nordisk did not deserve a preliminary injunction, having failed to show that Eli Lilly's ads threatened sales, undermined its goodwill, or caused lasting damage to its clinical reputation.   Quraishi called Novo Nordisk's claim of irreparable harm "inadequate to warrant the extraordinary relief it seeks." The judge ruled after a two-day hearing in late August.

Novo Nordisk sued Eli Lilly in July, saying ads for the obesity drug Zepbound and diabetes treatment Mounjaro violated federal and state false advertising and unfair competition laws by comparing higher doses of those products with lower doses of Novo Nordisk's Wegovy and Ozempic.   One commercial included a voiceover claim, with a written disclaimer, that people using Zepbound on average lost 50 pounds (23 kg) while people using Wegovy on average lost 33 pounds (15 kg). Also Read

GLP-1 boom in India, China, Brazil can create $22 bn market: JP Morgan

L'Oreal CEO says rise of weight-loss drugs impacting skincare consumption

Egg bites, Burger bowls: McDonald's tests protein-rich menu for GLP-1 users

Novo Nordisk aims to launch more than five blockbuster drugs by 2030: CEO

Mounjaro sales soar 502% as India's GLP-1 drug market expands rapidly

"While we are disappointed with the court's decision, today's ruling did not decide the question of whether Lilly's advertising is false and misleading, and this litigation is still ongoing," a Novo Nordisk spokesperson said in an email. "Everyone deserves clear, accurate and up-to-date information when making decisions about their health."

Eli Lilly, based in Indianapolis, has denied wrongdoing and said it was pleased with the decision.  WEIGHT-LOSS DRUGS ARE BIG BUSINESS   Weight-loss drugs have become major businesses for large pharmaceutical companies. The United States is among a handful of countries that allow direct-to-consumer advertising of prescription medicines.   In his 25-page decision, Quraishi said that while Novo Nordisk's witnesses were credible, Eli Lilly's ads had at most a negligible market impact between April and July, with prescriptions for Novo Nordisk's products remaining stable.   The judge said money damages could compensate Novo Nordisk for any "nontrivial harm" it might suffer absent an injunction.   Quraishi also found Novo Nordisk's case "less than persuasive" based on a "very preliminary record," though he did not rule on the merits.

Novo Nordisk reported combined sales of about $32 billion for obesity medicines and Ozempic in 2025, court papers show.   The drugmaker is working to regain market share in the United States for its injectable obesity drugs, a market projected to exceed $100 billion by the end of the decade.
